_comment: The growable-doc bounds (SPEC INV-234, ROADMAP row 392). Each of the five large working documents declares a byte ceiling with a recorded reason; the watcher guardrails/check-doc-bound.py (gate z) reds a doc past its ceiling with no rotation dated today and no raised bound. It composes with the doc-rotation gate (gate t, INV-209): crossing the bound earns a rotation, and rotation is the remedy the red points to. The ceilings were SEEDED 2026-07-18 with roughly a hundred kilobytes of rotation headroom each (measured then: PRODUCT_SPEC ~599 KB, ROADMAP ~603 KB, TEST_MATRIX ~345 KB, JOURNAL ~543 KB) so the gate would never red the already-large tree. That headroom is spent: on 2026-08-17 every ceiling was RATCHETED DOWN to the file's measured size, and the seeded headroom is gone. A doc that must grow now pays for the growth here by name, raising its number with a reason that says what was added and why rotation was not the remedy; the ratchet points down only. The four docs named in tests/test_doc_bound.py's FOUR_DOCS sit one byte under their ceiling because that test asserts the ceiling is strictly above the file; ARCHITECTURE.md, which that test does not cover, sits exactly at its ceiling. Bytes are the honest signal for the owner's cost — a guard's scan and a grep run slow with file size, named in kilobytes at ~18:25 on 2026-07-17.

PRODUCT_SPEC.md.reason: ratcheted down 2026-08-17 to 703126 — one byte above the file's measured 703125. It stood at 840000, raised 2026-07-20 for the back-describe migration (v3.0.0, INV-239/INV-217) when the Formal index gained its permanent Description column; that migration has long since landed and left 136875 bytes of unspent room, so the room is withdrawn. One byte above rather than exactly at the size, because tests/test_doc_bound.py asserts each of the four large docs sits strictly under its ceiling. Growth from here is paid for by name: raise this number with a reason that says what was added and why the closed portion could not rotate instead.

ROADMAP.md.reason: ratcheted down 2026-08-17 to 291721 — one byte above the body's measured 291720, taken AFTER that day's rotation moved the nine remaining terminal rows into docs/queue-archive/rotated-ROADMAP-2026-08.md. It stood at 700000, a stage number held above the ~603 KB pre-conversion body; its own reason said it would ratchet down once the body shrank to its live rows, and this is that ratchet. The queue rotates by the closing-commit law (SPEC INV-276, ROADMAP row 480): a row reaching a terminal exit moves to that month's archive in the same commit that closes it, so the live body stays the live queue and this ceiling is the backstop behind that habit. One byte above rather than exactly at the size, because tests/test_doc_bound.py asserts the strict inequality.

TEST_MATRIX.md.reason: ratcheted down 2026-08-17 to 484268 — one byte above the file's measured 484267. It stood at 530000, raised 2026-07-28 on a measurement over the live document: the matrix carries no row whose anchor has left PRODUCT_SPEC.md or ARCHITECTURE.md, so a rotation would move zero rows and free no bytes, and the document grew because the covered surface grew. That reading still holds — rotation is still the wrong remedy here — but the ~45 KB of headroom the raise carried is not earned by anything, so it is withdrawn and growth is paid for by name. One byte above rather than exactly at the size, because tests/test_doc_bound.py asserts the strict inequality.

JOURNAL.md.reason: ratcheted down 2026-08-17 to 373267 — one byte above the file's measured 373266. It stood at 640000, the 2026-07-18 seed above the then-current size with rotation headroom; the July chapters rotated to docs/queue-archive/JOURNAL-archive-2026-07-29.md and the headroom went unspent, so it is withdrawn. Old dated chapters keep rotating to a dated archive; a session that must write more than the ceiling allows rotates first or raises this number with a reason. One byte above rather than exactly at the size, because tests/test_doc_bound.py asserts the strict inequality.

ARCHITECTURE.md.reason: raised 2026-08-18 from 107652 to 107774, the file's measured size exactly, for 122 bytes of which not one is content. The ratchet's down-only rule is a law about what a document SAYS, not about how long the paths inside it are, and both of that night's additions are path length. The first, 48 bytes: six guardrail checks were parked in guardrails/attic/, and the eight places here that aim at them — six pins and two prose mentions — each gained the six characters of `attic/`. The second, 74 bytes: six pins into the spec-author skill were re-aimed at paths inside references/ after that skill's sections moved there. Both are the price of tidying up, and this field exists for exactly that. No word of architecture was added in either, and no node could have held the growth instead, because the growth IS the pins staying true to where their files now sit. The budget row's live test count was also refreshed twice that night, 2,506 to 2,532 to the 2,555 the merged tree collects; every one of those figures is the same width, so the refreshes cost nothing. No margin beyond the measured size was taken. Before that: ratcheted down 2026-08-17 to 107652, the file's measured size exactly. This entry never carried headroom: seeded 2026-08-15 for the readability milestone of the accepted plan v2 (2026-08-14) at that day's measured 107845, on the stated convention that the ceiling is the measured size and the ratchet points down only. The file has since shrunk by 193 bytes, so the ceiling follows it down. Exactly at the size rather than one byte above, because ARCHITECTURE.md is not among tests/test_doc_bound.py's FOUR_DOCS and the gate itself tolerates equality. The four large documents got a hundred kilobytes of room because they were already past reading size and rotation was the remedy; the architecture is still readable at ~105 KB, and the milestone's whole point is that it stays that way. A node that must grow pays for the growth here, by name: raise this number with a reason that says what was added and why no node could hold it instead.
